title: Window's phone validator diverges from the wizard's and writes an impossible number
method: ran both validators on the same inputs, then drove gui.run() through a widget-layer stub

must_not_contain: not a number any carrier will dial

observed_at_discovery: gui._phone_ok accepts any 10 or 11 digits; wizard.a_phone accepts 11 only when the first digit is 1. For '0307-555-0142' the terminal wizard returns "That doesn't look like a 10-digit phone number..." while the window accepts it and writes "phone": "+03075550142" -- no country code begins with 0. Same class as the already-fixed FS-1 hour-parser duplication; the hour validator was fixed by importing, the phone pair was left copied. pytest exit 1, 4 failed 6 passed.
